flawed_step: Triangle-free does not imply 3-colorable; triangle-free graphs can have chromatic number 4.
counterexample: Let indices be modulo 5. Take vertices v_0,...,v_4,u_0,...,u_4,w. Add edges v_i v_{i+1}, u_i v_{i-1}, u_i v_{i+1}, and wu_i for every i. This graph is triangle-free: the v_i induce C5; the u_i are independent; w has only u_i as neighbors; and the two v-neighbors of each u_i are nonadjacent. It is not 3-colorable: if a 3-coloring existed, rename colors so w has color 3. Every u_i then has color 1 or 2. For each v_i of color 3, recolor it with the color of u_i. This produces a proper 2-coloring of the induced C5, since u_i is adjacent to both neighbors of v_i. But C5 is not bipartite, a contradiction.
assessment_summary: The explicit 11-vertex Mycielski graph of C5 satisfies every hypothesis but requires four colors.
